newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-RHODES HITS 156 NOT OUT AS NATAL DOMINATE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-RHODES HITS 156 NOT OUT AS NATAL DOMINATE.

text.p: A career-best 156 not out from
Jonty Rhodes helped Natal take a firm grip of their Supersport
Series cricket match against Free State at Kingsmead on Sunday.
Rhodes, whose last test for South Africa was against India
in Ahmedabad last November, reminded the national selectors of
his batting temperament as he occupied the crease for just under
six hours without giving a chance.
Playing confidently on a flat pitch against a Free State
attack without the services of Franklyn Stephenson (hamstring
strain), he struck 15 fours and three sixes and faced 285 balls.
Natal, overnight 120 for two, were able to bat on until nine
overs after tea before eventually declaring their second innings
closed at 349 for seven.
This set Free State a daunting victory target of 472 from a
minimum of 130 overs. By the close of the third day, the
visitors had reached a comfortable 68 without loss in their
second innings run-chase, with Free State captain Gerhardus
Liebenberg unbaten on 29 and left-handed opener Deon Jordaan on
37 not out.
But the fluent batting of Jonty Rhodes was the undoubted
highlight of the day, and particularly while he dominated an
unbroken partnership of 124 for the eighth wicket with Doug
Watson (33 not out).
Watson, usually an opener, batted at nine because of a
broken left hand and provided an ideal foil to the positive
strokeplay of Rhodes against a Free State attack waiting for the
imminent Natal declaration.
The 27-year-old Rhodes reached his sixth first-class century
from 221 balls and went on to beat his previous career-best of
135 not out achieved against Border in Pietermaritzburg in
"I really enjoyed it out there as it was beautiful to bat on
today. My concentration was good - I think my first false stroke
was when I edged Chris Craven for four on 140," Rhodes said.
"My biggest problem with my batting has always been to
premeditate shots when I've reached 30 or 40 but today I made
sure they were always going to have to work hard to get my
wicket.
"I'm feeling a lot more relaxed with my batting now but I
haven't set my sights on getting back into the South African
team - if I did, I could get disappointed. Obviously it's my
goal to play for South Africa but it's also my goal to enjoy
myself - ad today I enjoyed myself."
